subject: Consumption lanes & gradual capacity onboarding — PilotEdge MAP draft
messages:
From: Alex Shaw <alex@pilotedge.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great overview of the serving guarantees. We discussed putting together a MAP that lets us start small, validate latency/cost for our customer use case, and then scale predictably.

High-level ask from our side: we need a plan that ties progressive consumption thresholds to pricing breaks and a hard close by end of Q3 (we've got internal procurement timelines). Specifically:
- Month 1 (pilot): up to 10M tokens — evaluation pricing
- Month 2–3 (validation): target 30M TPM average (monthly peak tolerance)
- Month 4+: commit to 120M tokens/month or agree on a staged commit cadence

Can you propose a MAP that:
1) spells out acceptance criteria for each phase (latency p95, error rate),
2) ties discount milestones to achieved TPM buckets, and
3) includes an opt-in for a one-time onboarding credit if we hit the earlier bucket?

Also attaching our internal acceptance checklist to help align. Goal is to be contract-ready by 8/25 so we can go live early September.

Appreciate a quick sketch so I can preview with procurement.

—Alex
PilotEdge — Head of Platform

Attachment: PilotEdge_acceptance_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Shaw <alex@pilotedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. High level we can support a lanes-based MAP that moves from evaluation -> verification -> committed capacity. Attached is a first-draft MAP that maps your buckets to performance SLAs and discount levers.

Key points in the draft:
- Pilot month (eval): up to 12M tokens, standard eval pricing, telemetry access + 1 week of dedicated SRE office hours for onboarding.
- Validation phase (month 2–3): target 25–40M tokens/month; if p95 latency < 220ms and error rate < 0.5% for two consecutive weeks, we apply an early uplift credit (one-time) and +10% discount on next month.
- Commitment phase (month 4+): two-tier commit options — a 120M/month commit (preferred) or a staircase commit that grows 40M/month over three months. Higher discounts (15–25%) tied to longer term commit and upfront payment.

Open items for pricing: whether PilotEdge wants a hard lower-bound (true minimum commit) or a flexible staircase; both approaches have different credit/true-up mechanics.

Can Ben and I sync on a version that exposes clearly the acceptance gates and the billing true-up flow? If we align, I can turn this into a Docusign-ready exhibit and aim for 8/25 contract execution.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: PilotEdge_MAP_v0.3.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Marissa — nice structure. A couple of immediate commercial clarifications from my side:
1) Billing cadence: do they want calendar-month billing or bill-from-go-live? I recommend calendar-months for clarity with procurement.
2) True-up: for the staircase option we need a simple true-up formula — e.g., if they commit to 40M then 80M then 120M, any underutilization in a month invokes an overage true-up at a blended rate (list - tier discount).
3) Credits: propose onboarding credit as a fixed $25k credit applied against first two invoices if they meet validation gates. Keeps math simple.

Jonas — can you double-check the latency p95 target vs our Dedicated slab on west-us? I want to make sure the 220ms target is realistic at 25–40M tokens/month. If not, propose a fallback (e.g., 280ms plus additional SRE-run tuning window).

I'll draft the pricing table once Jonas confirms perf.

—Ben
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Ben / Marissa — quick perf note after checking our west-us Dedicated pool:
- At baseline 32k-48k TPM sustained (mixed seq lengths), p95 ~ 210-240ms depending on prompt composition.
- For predictable p95 < 220ms at 40M/month we should reserve a 10% buffer capacity and enable prefix caching for predictable prompts. That means a modest uplift to the reserved capacity cost (~+8%).

Recommendation: keep 220ms as the target but note a conditional capacity buffer line in the MAP ("+8% reserved capacity uplift if validation traffic matches expected distribution"). This will be a transparent lever in the MAP.

Also: we'll include an SLA appendix that defines measurement windows and acceptable sampling for p95 calculation.

—Jonas
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Shaw <alex@pilotedge.com>, PilotEdge Commercial Team <procure@pilotedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Alex — attaching updated MAP that incorporates Ben/Jonas feedback. Short summary of the changes:
- Billing: calendar-month billing starting from go-live month.
- Two commit paths preserved: (A) Fixed commit — 120M/month with 20% discount for annual prepay; (B) Staircase — 40M -> 80M -> 120M over 3 months with true-up at the end of each calendar month.
- Onboarding credit: $25k credit applied to first two invoices if validation gates are met.
- Capacity buffer clause: +8% reserved capacity uplift if validation traffic profile requires it (documented measurement method in SLA appendix).
- Acceptance gates: explicit p95 and error rate checks defined; acceptance requires two consecutive weeks of signals inside thresholds.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can procurement confirm whether PilotEdge prefers Fixed commit (A) or Staircase (B)?
2) If Staircase, confirm whether you want the one-time onboarding credit or prefer a higher ongoing discount at final commit.
3) Please confirm target execution date — we are holding 9/1 as a possible go-live if contract is signed by 8/25.

I'll stand by to prepare the exhibit for signatures once you confirm path.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: PilotEdge_MAP_v0.4.pdf

From: Alex Shaw <alex@pilotedge.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: PilotEdge Commercial Team <procure@pilotedge.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotEdge pilot — proposed MAP lanes and monthly commitments

Marissa / Ben — we've reviewed with procurement and finance. Quick answers:
- We prefer Staircase (B) to limit initial cash outlay.
- We accept the $25k onboarding credit applied to the first two invoices (helps close internal approvals).
- We acknowledge the capacity buffer clause; pilot engineering will share traffic samples by EOD Monday so Jonas can validate the +8% uplift trigger.
- Target: aiming for contract signature week of 8/23 and go-live 9/1 — procurement asks for one minor change: a mutual termination clause with a 30-day notice during the first 90 days of the pilot (we can revert to standard 60-day thereafter).

If you can update the MAP with that mutual termination line, we can route for signatures. Appreciate the fast turn.

—Alex
Head of Platform, PilotEdge
